angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 431,334 km at 178.63 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.5981 +/- 0.0214 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10): 178.63 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.62 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Kanodia et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-3757 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...81K/abstract): 431,334 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.64 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Kanodia et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-3757 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...81K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3913 +/- 56 K from Kanodia et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-3757 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...81K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Kanodia et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-3757 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...81K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-3757.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.659, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
